clue.text: Passage checked by tall male, an old robber

indicators.note: a passage checked by others is held in, so WAY is enclosed by the words for tall and male

parts.note: tall means high
a male is a man
a way is a passage or route

explanation.surface: A corridor blocked by a tall man, who turns out to be a robber of old.
explanation.definitionFit: A highwayman was a mounted thief who held up travellers on the roads in past centuries.

clue.text: Campaigner, more coarse when held up

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the reversed word sits within the other

parts.note: more coarse means cruder

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word is reversed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A campaigner who becomes ruder when obstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' reads as delayed; split, 'held' signals the container and 'up' the reversal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Painstaking? All except us in workroom

indicators.note: all except a part means the whole word with that part removed

parts.note: painstaking means studious, careful and diligent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether everyone but us is diligent at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist or craftsperson works.

clue.text: Fine work of art, attractive

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate, a work of art

explanation.surface: Praising a fine artwork as attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching is an adjective meaning charming or good-looking.

clue.text: Basic piece of wire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... food or item is a basic, main one
second meaning: a bent piece of wire for fastening paper

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something fundamental and a noun for a small U-shaped fastener.

clue.text: Went fast through underpass, pedalling

indicators.note: the answer runs through the words, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: A cyclist racing along an underpass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, meaning moved quickly.

clue.text: Row right after dead heat

indicators.note: right comes after dead heat, so its letter is placed at the end

parts.note: a dead heat is a tie

explanation.surface: A rowing race ending in a dead heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another, as in a stadium.

clue.text: Sort of parade in New York? Watch recording

definitions.text: Sort of parade in New York?

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: Suggests watching a recording of a New York parade.
explanation.definitionFit: New York celebrates heroes with ticker-tape parades, showering them with paper strips from office windows.

clue.text: Men in Met cheered going off for a drink

indicators.note: going off means exploding or departing from the normal state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans at the Met, the New York opera house, cheering a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN, MET and CHEERED go into one pool of letters, with 'in' simply joining the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme de menthe is a sweet green mint liqueur.

clue.text: Engraved metal sought

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... metal has been decorated by engraving or embossing
second meaning: pursued or sought after

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a metalworking term for ornamenting a surface and also the past tense of pursue in its sense of hunting.

clue.text: Lark's flight across a delta

indicators.note: flight laid across the two letters means it spans them, holding them inside

parts.note: flight can mean escape, fleeing
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A songbird flying across a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' looks like the bird whose flight is described; it is the definition, meaning a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, and an escapade is an adventurous prank.

clue.text: Hotel, even more attractive

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
'and some' is an informal phrase meaning and even more

explanation.surface: Praising a hotel that is even more attractive than another.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking, pleasing to the eye.

clue.text: Peninsula in Russian region, not small

indicators.note: not small means the letter for small is taken away

parts.note: Siberia is the vast Asian region of Russia
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A peninsula found in Russia, though not a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the peninsula in south-west Europe shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: One may be used to exercise in a Delhi gym perhaps

definitions.text: One may be used to exercise in a Delhi gym perhaps

parts.words: One may be used to exercise in a Delhi gym perhaps
parts.note: read literally, a gym in Delhi is a club in India; the thing named is also a piece of exercise equipment

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the item, then hints at its name: a gym in Delhi would be a club in India.
explanation.definitionFit: These are bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in sets for strength and coordination training.

clue.text: Remind general about a German opera

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a jumble, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction to jog a general's memory regarding a German opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is not the nationality: Edward German was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrie England is a 1902 comic opera by the English composer Edward German.

clue.text: August place in danger housing army's leader

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the leader's letter goes within

parts.note: to imperil is to place in danger

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of army's

explanation.surface: A place threatened while sheltering an army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' with its capital looks like the month; it is the adjective meaning grand and stately.
explanation.definitionFit: August and imperial both describe something majestic and commanding respect, befitting an emperor.

clue.text: Fire-raiser on stairs, running

indicators.note: running suggests something in motion and in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone who starts fires fleeing up the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist deliberately sets fire to property, a fire-raiser in British legal language.

clue.text: Eagerly purchase crack at university

parts.note: a snap is a crack, a sharp breaking sound
up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student keen to buy something at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap up is to buy quickly and eagerly, like a bargain.

clue.text: Mate entertaining the Spanish with a rice dish

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: pal is a word for a mate or friend
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A friend hosting Spaniards and serving a rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish dish of saffron rice with seafood or meat.

clue.text: English celebrity describing our new rail service

indicators.note: describing can mean drawing around, as a circle is described, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: new indicates the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An English celebrity talking about a new train service.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed train service linking London with Paris and Brussels through the Channel Tunnel.

clue.text: Aloof concerning test on vehicle ending in failure

parts.note: re means concerning, about
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for vehicles in Britain

indicators.note: ending in means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of failure

explanation.surface: Someone distant about a car test that ended in failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote describes someone distant and detached in manner, as aloof does.

clue.text: Film based on fact — it follows King George

indicators.note: it follows King George, so its letters come after GR

parts.note: true means factual
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A historical film about the reign of King George.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a 1969 Western film starring John Wayne, remade in 2010.

clue.text: Genuine old Spanish coin

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a former silver coin of Spain

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for authentic and the name of a historic Spanish currency unit.

clue.text: Soldiers facing great danger

indicators.note: soldiers facing great puts the two pieces side by side, soldiers first

parts.note: men are soldiers, especially ordinary ranks
ace means excellent, great

explanation.surface: Troops confronting a great peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat, something that poses a danger.

clue.text: A group of owls initially plagued a busy terminal

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter
busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Owls swarming a crowded transport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is the collective noun for owls, as a flock is for sheep.

clue.text: Stagger round the bend on the way back

indicators.note: going the way back means travelling in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: round the bend is British slang for mad, nuts

explanation.surface: Someone lurching round a bend on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round the bend' reads like a road; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish them, to stun them.
